title: Surgical rollback and contextual backport guidelines for patch channeling
creator: Jin Park
description:
Goal: Define a deterministic, low-risk process for surgical rollbacks and targeted backports across active release channels (stable, LTS, and patch lanes). This doc formalizes severity criteria, branch naming and patch selection, automated gates for rollouts, required test coverage for hotfix merges, and a minimal human approval flow for P0/P1 patches.

Scope: hosts runtime, API, and dedicated deployment code that can require emergency fixes (not infra-only, not customer data migrations). Covers: severity definitions, patch branch workflow, cherry-pick rules, automated validation pipeline, canary/gradual rollout gates, rollback triggers and noise suppression, post-deploy verification checklist, communication templates, and cross-team handoffs.

Severity matrix (contextual):
- S0 (Critical - live data loss / security exploit): immediate freeze, patch branch created, emergency PR, 2x senior eng + security signoff, auto-priority patch merge, immediate global rollback capability if post-deploy monitors fire. Backport: to all supported LTS and stable channels within 24h.
- S1 (High - service outage, severe customer impact): hotfix pipeline with expedited reviews (1x senior eng + PM). Canary at 1% for 15 minutes, lifecycle monitoring. Backport: LTS channels if customers affected.
- S2 (Medium - degraded correctness/perf for subset): targeted patch and staged rollout; prefer feature-flag/gating change over code revert. Backport: evaluate based on regression window.
- S3/S4 (Low - cosmetic or rare): schedule in next normal patch release cycle, no emergency backport.

Patch branch & naming conventions:
- Create explicit patch branch from the release tag: patch/<release>-hotfix/<ticket>-<short-desc> e.g., patch/1.20-hotfix/ENG-135678-kv-cache-boundary.
- Use single logical change per patch branch. If multiple unrelated fixes are required, create separate branches and independent PRs.
- Include changelog header and affected-channel metadata in PR description: {"channels":"stable,lts-1.20"} (plain text in the PR body).

Backport policy (contextual approach):
- Prefer selective backporting: backport only to channels where the bug is active and customer-impacting. Blanket backports increase risk and test cost.
- Backport decision matrix: customer-reported AND non-workaroundable => backport to all supported channels where release contains the buggy commit. Non-customer internal regression => evaluate; prefer release-internal patch.
- Cherry-pick rules: use the backport-bot to create PRs from original patch branch; validate conflict resolutions in a local branch and document manual edits in PR description.

Automated validation pipeline (required for hotfix merges):
- Pre-merge: unit tests + smoke + impacted-service integration smoke. For S0/S1: run the fast subset of end-to-end (E2E-light) covering the failure mode.
- Post-merge/build: build artifact tagged with patch id, run canary deployment to canary pool for 15 min. Post-canary automated checks: error-rate, latency (p95), KV-cache-miss-rate, memory OOM monotonic checks.
- Health-check gating: use rollout-controller to block further rollout if any anomaly crosses alert thresholds for 3 consecutive checks. Automatic rollback will be initiated if rule threshold hit and human on-call ack absent after 2 minutes.

Rollout gates and incremental deployment plan:
- Canary: 1% for 15 minutes, observe metrics and logs.
- Ramp: 5% for 30 minutes, then 25% for 30 minutes, then remaining 69%. Each stage has automated checks and a human approval timeout (default 20 minutes).
- Rapid bypass: For S0 approved by execs, we allow a rapid global rollout but require a postmortem within 48 hours.

Automated rollback triggers and controls:
- Triggers: synthetic check failure, user-error-rate > baseline+3 sigma, memory error class, persistent OOM across >5 nodes, or data-corruption signal.
- Safety: automatic rollback performed by rollout-controller to the prior stable artifact. If rollback fails twice, the system pauses and alerts #oncall and #release-ops.
- Rollback tagging: create rollback/ENG-135678-<timestamp> branch with a short postmortem note.

Testing & observability requirements before approval:
- Must include reproduction steps, minimal repro harness or smoke script, and a numeric regression expectation (e.g., reduce p99 latency by X% or fix exception count Y->0).
- Dashboards: include a dedicated hotfix dashboard link in PR (Latency / Error / KV cache / Memory), and a link to canary logs.

Approvals & communication:
- P0: 2 senior eng approvals + PM + security (if security-related).
- P1: 1 senior eng + PM.
- P2+: peer review.
- Communication: open ticket in #oncall with subject "HOTFIX ENG-<id>: <summary>", tag oncall, post release notes to #releases post-deploy and list backported channels.

Tooling & automation improvements to deliver in this ticket:
- Backport-bot enhancements: auto-create cherry-pick PRs for selected channels and label with target channel.
- Rollout-controller: add a configurable human-approval timeout per-stage and faster rollback ack path.
- Patch branch lint: pre-merge lint to ensure changelog header and canary dashboard links present.

Open trade-offs and open questions:
- Trade-off: aggressive blanket backports reduce customer exposure but increase release engineering load and risk of introducing regressions into stable branches. We adopt a contextual approach to limit blast radius.
- Question: how long should we keep an emergency patch support window open for backports? Proposal: 30 days after patch for LTS owners to opt-in, after which changes go through normal release cycles.

Next steps for this ticket:
1) Ship a PR with the decision matrix + templates for PR body and Slack communication (ETA: 3d).
2) Implement patch branch lint in CI (ETA: 2 weeks).
3) Backport-bot change to create channel-targeted PRs (ETA: 3 weeks).
4) Run a tabletop drill with #oncall to validate rollback-controller triggers and human-ack flows (ETA: next cycle).
